 BHARATBHAI GANGARAM PATEL  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR.

Appearance:
MR ZUBIN F BHARDA(159) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 DS AFF.NOT FILED (N) for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MR ADIL R MIRZA(2488) for the Respondent(s) No. 2 PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. Rule returnable forthwith.

Learned APP waives service of notice of rule for and on behalf of the respondent-State and learned advocate Mr. Adil Mirza waives service of notice of rule for and on behalf of the respondent No.2-original complainant.
2.

By this application under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,1973, the applicant seeks to invoke the inherent powers of this Court praying for quashing of the first information report being C.R. No.I-123 of 2016 registered before the Pardi Police Station at Valsad for the offence punishable under sections 465, 467, 468, 471, 420 and 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code.

3. The facts, in brief, leading to the filing of the present application, are that the impugned FIR has been filed by the complainant Sunilkumar Paragjibhai Desai stating that he as well as his brother Nileshbhai and his two aunts, namely, Induben and Manjulaben were the owners of the agricultural land bearing Survey No.657/1, admeasuring 0-38-45 Hectors, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22335/2016 ORDER DATED: 12/07/2024 undefined situated in village Tukwada.
It is alleged in the complainant that his brother and his aunts are residing abroad since many years.

It is also alleged that upon the death of one of his aunts, namely, Induben, he undertook the procedure for effecting the inheritance entries in the revenue record, upon which, he came to know that the Bharatbhai Gangaram Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50250060/
1

entities.text: Bharatbhai Gangaram Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: aforesaid agricultural land had already been converted into non-agricultural land, which was also transferred in the name of one Ramakant Jagdishprasad Tibhrewala, Director of Roha Agricultural Developments Pvt. Ltd..

Therefore, the complainant obtained the relevant revenue records,
whereupon he came to know that one Jayesh Ishwarlal Desai, a resident of Mumbai had created a forged power of attorney in the name of the four owners on 14.02.2007, which neither contain the photographs nor signatures nor the thumb impression of any of the four owners and also had also affixed the bogus photographs of some other persons, and on the basis of the said forged power of attorney, the said Jayesh Ishwarlal Desai sold the land in question to one Vijuben @ Vijayaben Bharatbhai Patel by way of registered sale deed.

The said Vijuben @ Vijayaben Bharatbhai Patel, in turn, sold the said land to one Soha Agriculture Developers Pvt. Ltd. through its Director Ramakant Jagdishbhai Tibhrevalal on 07.03.2007 by way of registered sale deed for the total sale consideration of Rs.1,10,000/-.
With this sort of allegations, the impugned FIR has been lodged.

4. Learned advocate Mr. Zubin Bharda appearing for the applicant submits that the applicant herein is the husband of Vijuben @ Vijayaben Patel who is a bonafide purchaser of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22335/2016 ORDER DATED: 12/07/2024 undefined land bearing Survey No.657/1 who purchased the said land from the original owners including the complainant by executing a registered sale deed on 07.03.2007.

Learned advocate Mr. Bharda further submits that the land in question was purchased by the wife of the applicant upon payment of sale consideration by way of a cheque bearing No.013363 dated 07.03.2007 to the tune of Rs.1,10,000/-.
He also submits that the applicant-accused does not have any nexus with the allegation of forging of the power of attorney by one Jayesh Ishwarlal Desai.
The land was purchased by the wife of the applicant upon payment of total sale consideration of Rs.1,10,000/-.

Learned advocate Mr. Bharda further submits that after the execution of the sale deed in favour of the wife of the applicant, the land was converted to non-agricultural land and then sold out the said land along with other parcels of land to one company, namely, Soha Agriculture Developers Pvt. Ltd. by way of registered sale deed for the total sale consideration of Rs.55,00,000/-.
Learned advocate Mr. Bharda also submits that the applicant-accused has been falsely implicated in the present offence without there being any overt act disclosed or committed by the applicant.

The applicant- accused has not created any forged document and, therefore, no case is made out justifying investigation against the applicant-accused and, therefore, the impugned FIR is nothing but a sheer abuse of process of law filed by the complainant with malafide intention to harass the applicant-accused.

Even if the allegations levelled in the FIR are accepted in their entirety, without admitting the same, the same would not make out an offence as the applicant has merely witnessed the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22335/2016 ORDER DATED: 12/07/2024 undefined registered sale deed executed by Jayesh Ishwarlal Desai in favour of his wife.

5. Learned advocate Mr. Bharda also submits that the present FIR came to be lodged against four accused persons, and immediately after the registration of the FIR, the applicant- accused had approached this Court by filing the present application, and a Coordinate Bench of this Court, vide order dated 14.11.2016, protected the applicant-accused.

During the interregnum period, the investigation qua the other co- accused was proceeded with and, ultimately, at the end of investigation, charge-sheet also came to be filed against the other co-accused before the competent court.

After filing of the charge-sheet, the same was culminated into criminal case and the trial was Bharatbhai Gangaram Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50250060/
2

sentences.text: also proceeded with, and ultimately, at the end of day, after considering and appreciating all the materials available on record, the trial court has acquitted the other co- accused vide judgment and order dated 29.07.2021.
A copy of the said acquittal order has also been produced on record.

Learned advocate Mr. Bharda submits that even if the entire case of the first informant is accepted as true, none of the ingredients to constitute the offence of forgery are spelt out and, therefore, the continuation of the criminal proceedings against the applicant-accused would be nothing, but an abuse of the process of law.

6. Learned advocate Mr. Adil Mirza appearing for the original complainant submits that during the pendency of the present proceedings, the original complainant has passed away on 16.08.2022, a copy of the death certificate of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22335/2016 ORDER DATED:
12/07/2024 undefined complainant has also been produced on record by the learned advocate Mr.
Mirza, which is ordered to be taken on record.

He, therefore, submits that considering the above stated development in the matter, and without there being any further instructions in the matter, he is unable to make any further submissions in the matter and prays that appropriate order may be passed.

7. Learned APP Mr. Soham Joshi appearing for the respondent-State has opposed the present application and submits that the sale deed came to be executed in favour of the wife of the applicant-accused and ultimately the applicant- accused is also indirectly the beneficiary of the entire transaction.

He further submits that the said power of attorney itself is a forged one as the signatures, thumb impression as well as the photographs affixed thereon also do not belong to the complainant, his brother or his aunt.

Under the circumstances, learned APP Mr. Joshi prays that,
therefore, at this stage, the First Information Report should not be quashed and the trial should be permitted to proceed further.
Hence, the present application deserved to be rejected.
8. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and having considered the materials on record, the only question that falls for my consideration is whether I should quash the complaint.
9. I am conscious of the restrictions to be exercised by the Court of Law while considering the petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
However, in the matter on hand, I find that it is a clear cut case of abuse of process of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22335/2016 ORDER DATED: 12/07/2024 undefined law.

The records prima facie reveal that the allegations in the first information report are of forging the power of attorney in the name of the complainant as well as his brother and aunts by one Jayesh Ishwarlal Desai.
However, I fail to understand that in the entire episode of forgery, how the applicant- accused has played any role.

The accusations against the applicant-accused is that the land in question was sold to his wife by the power of attorney holder of the complainant and the applicant-accused has witnessed the registration of the sale deed and endorsed his signature upon the same, which the applicant-accused is not denying.
The wife of the applicant- accused seems to be the bona fide purchaser of the land in question, who purchased the land in question by paying the amount of sale consideration.
The record further reveals that the applicant-accused is not the purchaser of the land in question.
He has only witnessed the said transaction.
Moreover, the original purchaser, i.e., the wife of the applicant has not been named in the FIR.

Over and above the same, the other co-accused persons named in the Bharatbhai Gangaram Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50250060/
3 FIR including the one who has also endorsed his signature in the sale deed, have already been acquitted by the trial court from all the charges levelled against them and, therefore, now no fruitful purpose would be served to ask the applicant-accused to face the trial.
10.

sentences.text: The Supreme Court has, in the case of Mohammed Ibrahim and others vs. State of Bihar and another, reported in 2010 (1) GLH 184, very exhaustively explained as to what will constitute forgery.

entities.text: Mohammed Ibrahim and others vs. State of Bihar and another, reported in 2010 (1) GLH 184
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The ratio as propounded by the Supreme Court in the said case squarely applies in the case on NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22335/2016 ORDER DATED: 12/07/2024 undefined hand.

The relevant paragraphs are reproduced hereinbelow:
"10.

Section 467(in so far as it is relevant to this case) provides that whoever forges a document which purports to be a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine.

Section 471, relevant to our purpose, provides that whoever fraudulently or dishonestly uses as genuine any document which he knows or has reason to believe to be a forged document, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had forged such document.
Section 470 defines a forged document as a false document made by forgery.
The term "forgery" used in these two sections is defined in section 463.

Whoever makes any false documents with intent to cause damage or injury to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to part with property,
or to enter into express or implied contract, or with intent to commit fraud or that the fraud may be committed, commits forgery.

entities.text: Bharatbhai Gangaram Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: signed, sealed, executed or affixed; or Secondly.--Who, without lawful authority, dishonestly or fraudulently, by cancellation or otherwise, alters a document or an electronic record in any material part thereof, after it has been made, executed or affixed with digital signature either by himself or by any other person, whether such person be living or dead at the time of such alternation; or Thirdly.--Who dishonestly or fraudulently causes any person to sign, seal, execute or alter a document or an electronic record or to affix his digital signature on any electronic record knowing that such person by reason of unsoundness of mind or intoxication cannot, or that by reason of deception practised upon him, he does not know the contents of the document or electronic record or the nature of the alteration.
Explanation 1 - A man's signature of his own name may amount to forgery.

Explanation 2 - The making of a false document in the name of a fictitious person, intending it to be believed that the document was made by a real person, or in the name of a deceased person,
intending it to be believed that the document was made by the person in his lifetime, may amount to forgery.

NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22335/2016 ORDER DATED: 12/07/2024 undefined [Note: The words `digital signature' wherever it occurs were substituted by the words `electronic signature' by Amendment Act 10 of 2009]."
The condition precedent for an offence under sections 467 and 471 is forgery.
The condition precedent for forgery is making a false document (or false electronic record or part thereof).
This case does not relate to any false electronic record.

Therefore, the question is whether the first accused, in executing and registering the two sale deeds purporting to sell a property (even if it is assumed that it did not belong to him), can be said to have made and executed false documents, in collusion with the other accused.

14. An analysis of section 464 of Penal Code shows that it divides false documents into three categories:
1) The first is where a person dishonestly or fraudulently makes or executes a document with the intention of causing it to be believed that such document was made or executed by some other person, or by the authority of some other person, by whom or by whose authority he knows it was not made or executed.

2) The second is where a person dishonestly or fraudulently, by cancellation or otherwise, alters a document in any material part, without lawful authority, after it has been made or executed by either himself or any other person.

3) The third is where a person dishonestly or fraudulently causes any person to sign,
execute or alter a document knowing that such person could not by reason of (a)
unsoundness of mind; or (b) intoxication; or (c) deception practised upon him, know the contents of the document or the nature of the alteration.

sentences.text: NEUTRAL

undefined In short, a person is said to have made a `false document', if (i) he made or executed a document claiming to be someone else or authorised by someone else; or (ii) he altered or tampered a document; or (iii) he obtained a document by practicing deception, or from a person not in control of his senses.
15. The sale deeds executed by first appellant, clearly and obviously do not fall under the second and third categories of `false documents'.

It therefore remains to be seen whether the claim of the complainant that the execution of sale deeds by the first accused, who was in no way connected with the land, amounted to committing forgery of the documents with the intention of taking possession of complainant's land (and that accused 2 to 5 as the purchaser, witness, scribe and stamp vendor colluded with first accused in execution and registration of the said sale deeds) would bring the case under the first category.

16. There is a fundamental difference between a person executing a sale deed claiming that the property conveyed is his property, and a person executing a sale deed by impersonating the owner or falsely claiming to be authorised or empowered by the owner, to execute the deed on owner's behalf.
When a person executes a document conveying a property describing it as his, there are two possibilities.
The first is that he bonafide believes that the property actually belongs to him.
The second is that he may be dishonestly or fraudulently claiming it to be his even though he knows that it is not his property.
But to fall under first category of `false documents', it is not sufficient that a document has been made or executed dishonestly or fraudulently.

There is a further requirement that it should have been made with the intention of causing it to be believed that such document was made or executed by, or by the authority of a person, by whom or by whose authority he knows that it was not made or executed.

17. When a document is executed by a person claiming a property which is not his, he is not claiming that he is NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22335/2016 ORDER DATED: 12/07/2024 undefined someone else nor is he claiming that he is authorised by someone else.
Therefore, execution of such document (purporting to convey some property of which he is not the owner) is not execution of a false document as defined under section 464 of the Code.
If what is executed is not a false document, there is no forgery.
If there is no forgery, then neither section 467 nor section 471 of the Code are attracted."

11. The Court cannot permit a prosecution to go on if the case falls in one of the categories as illustratively enumerated by the Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana vs. Bhajan Lal,
reported in (1992) Supp (1) SCC 335.

entities.text:
State of Haryana vs. Bhajan Lal,
reported in (1992) Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Judicial process is a solemn proceeding which cannot be allowed to be converted into an instrument of oppression or harassment.

When there are materials to indicate that a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive, the high court shall not hesitate in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to quash the proceeding.

Under category seven (7) as enumerated in Bhajan Lal (supra), it is held thus, "where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge".

There cannot be any dispute that the inherent power given to the High Court Bharatbhai Gangaram Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50250060/
6 under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is with a purpose and object of advancement of justice.

sentences.text: Similar observations are also made by the Apex Court in the case of Vineet Kumar and Others vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh and Another, reported in (2017) 13 SCC 369.

sentences.text:
The facts and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22335/2016 ORDER DATED: 12/07/2024 undefined circumstances of this case clearly attract category No.7 as quoted supra.
12.
In the result, this application succeeds and is allowed.

The first information report being C.R.
No.I-123 of 2016 registered before the Pardi Police Station at Valsad is hereby ordered to be quashed.
All consequential proceedings arising from the same also stands terminated.
Rule is made absolute.
Direct service is permitted.
